transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-02
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (CTO - Aurum), Dana Liu (ML Eng - Aurum), Raj Patel (DevOps - Aurum), Sofia Mendez (Security - Aurum)

Summary: (auto) Aurum is evaluating migration from OpenAI hosted to Redwood Dedicated / Private for cost predictability and data controls. Interested in eval parity, benchmarks against vLLM/TGI, and compliance integration.

---- Transcript ----
00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Alex from Redwood here, with Priya our SE. How's every— is that Michael?
00:06 Michael Torres: Yeah, hi Alex, thanks. Looks like sound is okay on our side.
00:09 Alex Chen: Great. Quick run of agenda, talk current stack, goals, constraints, then dig into tech bits and next steps. Priya can you intro?
00:17 Priya Kapoor: Sure, hi all. I'm Priya, senior solutions engineer. I've worked on migrations from OpenAI and Anthropic to Dedicated/private infra so happy to go through compatibility and benchmark planning.
00:27 Michael Torres: Appreciate it. Quick context: we run a multi-tenant SaaS for clinical insights, heavy token usage, around 300M tokens/month on OpenAI, costs spiking, tail latency sometimes causes timeouts in our pipeline. Also compliance—they want PII never leaving our VPC for some workloads.
00:45 Dana Liu: And from the ML side, we care about inference parity—prompts we use produce slightly different outputs on non-OpenAI runtimes, usually vLLM or TGI shows small drift. We need to know how Redwood handles model variants, quantization and KV cache so we can maintain eval scores.
01:05 Alex Chen: Totally. So high level Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, and a control plane. We also offer Private (VPC/on-prem) if you need full network isolation. Typical migration path is start with Dedicated for predictable cost and then evaluate Private for PII workloads.
01:24 Raj Patel: For networking, we need to understand VPC peering, egress rules, and if we can bring our own KMS/HSM for key management.
01:31 Sofia Mendez: Also audit logs and SOC2 controls, encryption at rest, SSO/SAML, RBAC.
01:37 Priya Kapoor: We can provide SOC2 docs and a security package. For KMS, Redwood supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations for Private; for Dedicated we offer KMS integration options—Alex will share specifics.
01:48 Michael Torres: On the compatibility front—our services are built on the OpenAI API. We want a minimal refactor. Is Redwood API OpenAI-compatible or will we need to change code?
01:58 Alex Chen: Redwood's SDKs are developer-first and we provide an OpenAI-compatible wrapper for common generation endpoints to ease migrations. There are some nuances: streaming semantics and tool-calling have small differences, but for most REST calls you can point to Redwood endpoints with minimal changes. Priya, want to add?
02:14 Priya Kapoor: Yeah, and we also surface model catalog names—if you're using gpt-4 style models we map to verified model variants. For embeddings and chat, our SDK aims to match OpenAI semantics but we recommend running an eval parity test since tokenization, sampling seeds, and quantization can cause small diffs.
02:31 Dana Liu: That aligns with what we saw with vLLM—it's often close but sampling randomness and kv cache handling matter; also quantized weights change completions slightly. What's Redwood's approach to quantization?
02:43 Priya Kapoor: We have quantization profiles optimized per model and workload; for Dedicated we let you pick lower precision to reduce cost or keep full precision for parity. There's also a mode where we run a fallback to a higher-precision variant if a quality regression is detected.
02:56 Michael Torres: Cool. For our compliance-sensitive pipelines we might need on-prem. How painful is the Private deployment?
03:03 Alex Chen: Private is heavier lift but we provide a packaged control plane and ops automation. Typical timeline 6-12 weeks depending on network, KMS, and audit gating. Many customers pilot on Dedicated first to validate eval parity and benchmark then move to Private.
03:17 Raj Patel: Benchmarks—we run both throughput and latency SLOs. Would Redwood run comparative benchmarks vs OpenAI and vLLM?
03:25 Priya Kapoor: Yes, we propose a benchmark plan: we'll run your prompt set against OpenAI, Redwood Dedicated, and a vLLM/TGI self-hosted baseline if you have it. We'll measure avg latency p50/p95/p99, token cost, and eval metrics like Rouge/BLEU or your custom utility metric. We'll also check KV cache hit rates and batching efficiency.
03:45 Dana Liu: For eval parity, our main metric is Rouge-L on generated summaries plus a downstream classification accuracy; small shifts can cascade. How do you handle model variants—do you guarantee same model weights?
03:56 Priya Kapoor: We onboard verified model checkpoints where possible. For open weights that's straightforward; for models behind licenses we provide closest compatible variants. We also run automatic regression tests against your eval set during rollouts and support canary deploys with automatic rollback on quality regressions.
04:14 Michael Torres: What about vLLM vs TGI differences—we saw TGI faster on some long context jobs but worse sampling behavior on others. Can Redwood support both runtimes?
04:24 Priya Kapoor: Our serving runtime abstracts kernel selection; we can run different backend kernels (e.g., vLLM-like optimizations or TGI) and choose based on sequence length and model architecture. For Dedicated we tune kernel configs and quantization to your workload. We'll include those parameters in the benchmark report.
04:40 Sofia Mendez: On security, can you attest to SOC2 and provide penetration test summaries? Also, data retention policies and ability to purge logs per request?
04:50 Alex Chen: Yes, SOC2 attestation and pen test summaries are part of our security pack. Logs can be configured—retention windows and purge policies available, and for Private you manage logs in your VPC. We'll share the docs after the call.
05:03 Michael Torres: Pricing—OpenAI is variable; we'd like committed pricing. How does Redwood Dedicated pricing look?
05:09 Alex Chen: Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity with monthly/annual commits. We provide sizing options: small/medium/large GPU pools with predicted throughput and amortized per-token cost. Alex will send an initial spreadsheet and assumptions.
05:20 Michael Torres: Great. If we do proof-of-concept, what does success look like?
05:24 Dana Liu: For ML success: parity within a small delta on Rouge and downstream metric, and within 10% p95 latency target. For engineering: minimal refactor, stable throughput, and cost savings versus OpenAI. For security: acceptance of KMS and SOC2 controls.
05:40 Alex Chen: Sounds reasonable. We'll propose a POC: 2-week bench on Dedicated, run your 200-sample eval set, and compare. If results look good we proceed to sizing and Private evaluation.
05:50 Raj Patel: Network question—do you support private link / VPC peering so data doesn't traverse public internet?
05:57 Priya Kapoor: Yes, we support VPC peering and private link style connections for Dedicated and Private options. We'll capture network requirements in the follow-up doc.
06:07 Michael Torres: One concern—does Redwood throttle or change sampling behavior due to batching optimizations? We need deterministic-ish behavior for reproducibility.
06:17 Priya Kapoor: Batching can affect latency but not the sampling algorithm—however continuous batching and prefix KV caching can change timings; for determinism we can run a dedicated low-latency lane with smaller batch sizes and fixed seeds for sampling in tests. We'll document the tradeoffs.
06:32 Dana Liu: About tokenizer differences—OpenAI tokenization vs other tokenizers sometimes leads to token accounting diffs. Can you confirm tokenization parity?
06:40 Alex Chen: We use compatible tokenizers for verified models; we also provide tokenization tools in the SDK so you can reproduce token counts locally. We'll validate tokenization as part of the eval suite.
06:52 Michael Torres: Any gotchas migrating function-calling or tool-calling flows? We rely on structured outputs a lot.
06:59 Priya Kapoor: Function-calling semantics are supported but some vendors have slightly different wire formats. Redwood supports structured output and function/tool calling; we recommend a short integration test for edge cases.
07:10 Sofia Mendez: Regarding data residency, some of our customers require EU-only hosting. Do you provide region-specific Dedicated?
07:16 Alex Chen: Yes, Dedicated and Private can be provisioned in regions; we have EU regions and customer-managed Private for strict residency. We'll include region options in the pricing sheet.
07:25 Michael Torres: Timeline-wise, we'd like a pilot before end of Q4. Is that feasible?
07:30 Alex Chen: Feasible—if we get your eval set and agree on sizing this week, a 2-week Dedicated pilot could start mid-October, finishing before end of Q4. Priya, any blockers?
07:39 Priya Kapoor: Not from SE side; main blocker is receiving prompt set and defining acceptance criteria. Also need access for benchmarking endpoints—either sample payloads or a mock harness.
07:47 Dana Liu: We'll send sample prompts and eval metrics by Tuesday.
07:50 Alex Chen: Great. Next steps recap: I'll send pricing + SOC2 + KMS notes; Priya will draft benchmark plan; Dana and Raj will share artifacts.
07:59 Michael Torres: That works. Thanks everyone, excited to see the results.
08:03 Alex Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep-dive.
